idiom_name: enhanced for over Iterable, plus Iterable.forEach(Consumer)
implementation_notes: The enhanced for statement is the enumeration message: the compiler calls Iterable.iterator() on the operand (the JDK documents Iterable as the interface that 'allows an object to be the target of the enhanced for statement'), so any collection is walkable with one line and Iterable.forEach(Consumer) is the same walk as a message with a lambda. Since Java 8 the transforming siblings live in java.util.stream - map/filter/sorted/collect are lazy intermediate operations and forEach/count/sum are terminal ones - which also makes forEach a terminal step of a pipeline. Use the classic index loop only where the position is part of the computation; use iterator/forEach where elements are.
pitfalls: Removing elements while iterating throws ConcurrentModificationException (fail-fast iterators): use Iterator.remove(), Collection.removeIf, or collect the victims first.

The enhanced for cannot expose or change the index, so a walk that also needs the position stays a classic for loop - and indexing an ArrayList inside a loop (list.get(i)) that could have used an iterator is the classic accidental quadratic on LinkedList.
forEach(Consumer) cannot break out or return a value; a search that must stop belongs in a for loop or a short-circuiting stream operation (anyMatch/findFirst).

variants.name: Stream pipeline (map/filter/collect)
variants.implementation_notes: Java 8 adds the transforming messages as lazy pipelines: source.stream() then map/filter/sorted/collect, with forEach or a reduction as the terminal step; intermediate results are never materialised and parallel() re-targets the same pipeline onto a ForkJoinPool. Prefer it when enumeration produces a value or a collection, at the cost of a pipeline mental model, single-use streams and lambdas that must be stateless and non-interfering.
variants.code_sketch:
Map<String, Integer> bySku = order.lines().stream()
        .filter(OrderLine::isTaxable)
        .collect(Collectors.groupingBy(OrderLine::getSku,
                 Collectors.summingInt(OrderLine::getAmount)));
bySku.forEach((sku, total) -> report(sku, total));  // terminal message
pitfalls: A stream is consumed by its terminal operation: reusing the variable throws IllegalStateException, and most sources do not support concurrent structural modification while the pipeline runs.
forEach on a parallel stream gives no ordering guarantee and hides work in a ForkJoinPool; use forEachOrdered or collect when order or locality matters.
